clips.send: In 476 the Western Roman Empire fell. Over the next thousand years Europeans built castles and cathedrals, Constantinople kept Rome’s traditions alive, scholars in Baghdad translated the world’s books into Arabic — and a plague killed about a third of Europe in just a few years. Were these really the “Dark Ages”?
